## Ajouter votre plugin (2 minutes).content:
## Ajouter votre plugin (2 minutes)

1. Faites la recette une fois à la main.
2. `skill {"action": "save", "name": "ma-recette", "content": "# étapes\n1. ..."}`.
3. L'agent la rechargera seul quand la tâche ressemble.

# Unattended lifecycle regression tests.content:
# Unattended lifecycle regression tests — 13 September 2026

This follow-up uses fresh workspaces and one `Agent.runTurn` per trial. No game source is written by the supervising agent, and no follow-up repair prompts are sent into a trial. Independent checks run outside the generated workspace. A returned model answer is recorded separately from application acceptance.

## Final accepted results.content:
## Final accepted results

Both selected builds completed unattended and passed a fresh repeat of the same **30-check gate**: fifteen groups in the real smolcoder preview and fifteen in a direct browser. This includes Play, visible terrain/HUD, mesh quality, gravity/jumping, WASD at three headings, visible mining/placement, repeated pause/resume, manual Save and reload, New World followed by visible editing, and malformed-save recovery. Screenshots were inspected separately. No manual source fixes or agent restarts were used within either accepted trial.

| Provider and trial | Time | Coding requests / model tools | Own tests | Acceptance attempts during generation | Final independent repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Ollama v9 | 261 s | 65 / 63 | 28 passed | 2 | 30 passed |
| LM Studio v11 | 937 s | 187 / 195 | 23 passed | 5 | 30 passed |

The installed models were **Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M**, with a **65,536-token context** and reasoning off, run sequentially on an RTX 5090. Both trials used identical compiled harness and task-prompt hashes. Timing covers the agent turn and its checks; initial model loading is outside it. Ollama's original gate had fourteen preview groups; LM Studio's final trial required all thirty from launch. Both unchanged artifacts pass the final thirty-group gate, but their timings are not a controlled comparison. These selected successes follow the failures recorded below and do not establish a completion rate or superiority over another harness.

## Final accepted results::1.content:
Download the exact generated [Ollama source](evidence/ollama-v9-block-meadow.zip) and [LM Studio source](evidence/lmstudio-v11-block-meadow.zip). Extract either archive, run `npm ci`, then `npm run dev`. All archive entries match their source workspaces, and both clean extractions pass their own tests and production builds. The generated Vite 5 development toolchains retain their reported dependency advisories; they are preserved as benchmark records rather than silently repaired by the supervisor.

The [machine-readable evidence](evidence/unattended-2026-09-13.json) contains source/checker/harness hashes, original outcomes, acceptance attempts and final browser reports. Compressed complete [Ollama trace](evidence/ollama-v9-run.jsonl.gz) and [LM Studio trace](evidence/lmstudio-v11-run.jsonl.gz) retain the original requests, tools, results and compaction events. [Ollama gameplay](evidence/ollama-game.png) and [LM Studio gameplay](evidence/lmstudio-v11-game.png) show the accepted artifacts. Earlier archives below are explicitly historical or rejected.

The harness suite passed **107 tests, with one Windows symlink-privilege skip and no failures**. Browser observer fixtures separately cover preview permissions, confirmation handling, mesh validity, visible HUD state, caught errors, rendered edits and movement directions.

## Preview regression.content:
## Preview regression

Commit `1057acd` added iframe sandboxing without `allow-pointer-lock` or `allow-modals`. A first-person game could run directly but fail to leave its menu inside smolcoder. The previous browser test only exercised the direct URL and missed this regression.

`bench/preview-browser.cjs` reproduces the failure through the actual WebHub and browser client. Before the fix, pointer lock raised a browser exception and confirmation dialogs were suppressed. After enabling these two permissions, all four checks passed, including rejection of navigation to the hub origin. The existing Block Meadow artifact also passed all 13 gameplay check groups inside the real preview. No game implementation change was needed for this fix.

## Matched ungated trials.content:
## Matched ungated trials

The task is `bench/minecraft-lifecycle-prompt.txt`: a seeded voxel game with collision, editing, persistence, tests and a production build. Both backends use installed Qwen3.8 27B models labeled Q4_K_M, reasoning off, and a 32,768-token allocation. Their weight files have not been checked for byte identity. These are 27B-model tests, not evidence about 4B models or 8k windows. The providers run sequentially; the model loaded for a completed test is unloaded before switching providers.

The comparison checkout is `5e0346c`, immediately before the audit changes. The driver can load its compiled production code with `--harness=PATH`; no old-agent behavior is replaced by the driver. Trial outcomes are stochastic single samples, not completion-rate estimates.

| Trial | Model requests | Tool calls | Time | Independent outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| LM Studio, audit version | 155 | 158 | 710 s | Own tests/build pass; preview gameplay reaches Save, where the pause overlay intercepts the button. Fails acceptance. |
| LM Studio, previous checkout | 25 | 35 | 274 s | Claimed tests/browser checks without executing them. Independent tests: 19 pass, 7 fail; build passes; no usable Play button. Fails acceptance. |
| Ollama, audit version plus retained-read fix | 160 | 187 | 486 s | Tests/build and main gameplay pass; the then-current checker did not observe a New World reset. The confirmation adapter was subsequently corrected, so this is not a final-checker verdict. |

## Matched ungated trials::1.content:
| Ollama, previous checkout | 177 | 190 | 835 s | Advertised `npm test` fails; invoking the test files directly passes 19 tests and build passes. Browser starts, but terrain is invisible and the pause overlay blocks Save. Fails acceptance. |

The LM Studio comparison does not invalidate earlier successful games made with the previous harness. It shows why a fresh returned answer is insufficient evidence for this more demanding task.

## Changes under test.content:
## Changes under test

The first gated Ollama trial exposed a regression in `1057acd`'s write-payload eviction: it replaced old `write_file` arguments with a string describing omitted code. The model later copied that string into actual source files and spent many calls trying to recover. This trial was stopped and is not a passing result. The first fix turned completed large writes into plain assistant receipts and removed their paired tool results, preserving failed/pending calls and mixed batches. The final representation uses marked harness history records, as explained below. It never manufactures executable arguments. A narrow file-tool guard rejects the exact legacy marker without changing the file.

A second fresh Ollama trial with this fix and reasoning off did not reproduce placeholder corruption. It generated a world lookup that regenerated terrain repeatedly, making one terrain test take about 98 seconds. It repaired several assertion/data issues but repeated slow and timed-out test runs without resolving that cost. The supervising audit stopped this trial before browser acceptance; it is also not a passing result. Subsequent fresh trials use low reasoning. This is a configuration change, so they are not a controlled measurement of the acceptance gate alone.

The first low-reasoning LM Studio trial exhausted three 8,192-token replies entirely on reasoning. One response with thinking off recovered each time, but the repeated cost was substantial. That trial was stopped before completion. Repeated exhaustion now extends the announced recovery interval from one to four, then at most eight responses with thinking off before retrying the selected effort. The model preference is not changed, and the interval resets for a new user turn.

The next low-reasoning LM Studio trial spent many calls reconciling module interfaces, with small edits and evictions repeatedly resetting the individual read guards. It eventually ran tests and was repairing failures when the audit stopped it to install periodic project checks. It is not a completed result. The following fresh trials return to reasoning off, matching the ungated comparison setting.

## Changes under test::1.content:
The next LM Studio run completed its full attempt budget: 231 coding requests, 227 model tool calls, about 1,443 seconds, and six failed acceptance attempts. It automatically repaired build/test failures and block placement, but did not finish a working New World flow. Its buttons captured initial no-op callbacks instead of later callback assignments. Save/reload had passed via an unload auto-save, which was insufficient evidence that Save itself worked. This run is recorded as incomplete.

- `--verify COMMAND` is an explicit headless acceptance gate. The caller's command is immutable during the run and is not another model-visible tool schema. Failures return to the same running agent automatically, including when repeated tool attempts would otherwise pause it. The latest failed check survives compaction as actual evidence. Six acceptance attempts and the model-step budget bound retries; failure or cancellation exits nonzero.
- The repeated-read guard counts observations the model still has. Refetching an evicted result must not trigger a stop. The generic repeated-call guard follows the same rule.
- Without a caller-supplied command, the shared terminal/web/headless agent automatically discovers conventional Node `build`, `test`, and `test:e2e` scripts after file edits. Project-owned scripts only establish the behavior they test.
- After edits, those project scripts also run every 24 tool calls during implementation. Their actual failures survive compaction and return directly to the same agent; these progress checks are separate from the caller's final acceptance budget. This counters cycles of rereading and making small API changes before executing anything. A separate 24-read limit can request acceptance feedback after edits even when previous reads were evicted.
- Once final acceptance has failed, periodic checks use that acceptance command instead of weaker project checks. A green unit test cannot clear a browser failure. A final answer with no intervening tool activity reuses the just-passed acceptance result rather than spending another attempt.

## Changes under test::2.content:
- Background summarization waits 750 ms before inference. Quick shell checks finish without launching an immediately cancelled prefill; longer commands can still overlap with a summary.
- The preview permits pointer lock and confirmation dialogs.
- An earlier LM Studio trial left a backgrounded Vite process holding command pipes open after completion. Managed Bash commands now keep their shell alive while ordinary `&` jobs run, so cancellation can terminate the process tree on Windows. Cancellation and task stop also close inherited pipes. Two real-process regression tests fail before this fix and pass after it; the foreground exit code is preserved.

`bench/voxel-acceptance.cjs` runs the generated project's tests and build, serves the built output with `vite preview`, and runs `bench/voxel-browser.cjs` through the real smolcoder preview. It returns the first failure to keep repair feedback focused. It never edits the generated game. Logs and independent acceptance code stay outside the generated workspace. Earlier comparison browser runs used the dev server; the final gated trials validate the production bundle.

The browser checks cover startup, Play/pointer lock, a nonblank rendered game canvas, gravity and jumping, all WASD keys, five hotbar selections, mouse targeting/mining, adjacent placement, pause/resume twice, persistence of actual edited cells and player state, and rejecting/accepting New World. Debug teleport arranges positions; keyboard and mouse perform gameplay. The generic test uses the platform's pointer-unlock API because headless Chrome does not consistently handle its native Escape accelerator; it does not set game pause state. The existing artifact's dedicated suite additionally exercises Escape itself.

## Changes under test::3.content:
The checker was refined during the audit, and older partial results are not presented as final passes. Input checks hold Space across a frame, observe hotbar selection after two frames, and allow the asynchronous pointer-unlock event to settle. Setup teleports above the actual terrain and waits for landing instead of assuming a fixed height or frame rate; view-angle scans find a reachable target, and placement aims away from the player's body.

The final checker explicitly requires the menu to disappear after Play. It clears only the isolated test browser's game storage before clicking Save, requires a write before navigation, and verifies that Play preserves the restored position. It handles native and HTML confirmation dialogs, checks that resetting changes actual edited terrain rather than just a counter, and exercises movement after New World. Both confirmation adapters pass an independent browser fixture. The existing working game passed this complete production-preview lifecycle three consecutive times (`control-stable-1` through `control-stable-3`). Each report hashes the checker and its support scripts. Failure feedback omits inaccessible diagnostic-file paths, which had distracted the model from project repairs.

Ollama trial `verified-v3` exposed another checker defect: the prompt described snapshot contents without prescribing field names, while the checker expected `selected` and the game exposed `selectedBlock`. Five acceptance attempts included repeated false hotbar failures and one subsequent source error. The trial was stopped and is not valid reliability evidence. The checker now accepts these field aliases, and the prompt specifies the exact snapshot schema for new trials. The working control passed all 12 groups again (`control-schema`). The final trials use this revised prompt and checker; they are not a controlled measurement against the earlier ungated samples.

## Changes under test::4.content:
Ollama `verified-v4` exposed a remaining problem in the receipt representation. Three replies copied synthetic `Completed write_file`/`Completed edit_file` prose without executing those tools. The record had been placed in an assistant message, teaching an answer pattern that did not perform work. This trial was stopped during test repairs. Receipts now appear as explicitly marked harness history in user-role data, separate from actual assistant replies and paired tool results. Their metadata excludes them from user-turn detection and reasoning boundaries. Regression tests cover those roles, boundaries, mixed batches and retained source warnings. The next runs use this correction.

LM Studio `verified-v4` then reached its six-attempt limit without crashing: 155 coding requests, 174 model tool calls and 663 seconds. It automatically fixed a missing startup call, then save/reload persistence. Ten browser groups passed; the last two acceptance attempts failed at movement after New World. Source inspection confirmed a game defect: reset replaced `this.game`, while the input handler retained the old game object. The game source was not manually repaired. The run exited nonzero and remains an incomplete result.

Ollama `verified-v5` also ended incomplete at six checks: 181 coding requests, 181 model tool calls and 606 seconds. It repaired collision and an overlay blocking Save, then reached a save/reload edit-count failure. Its first browser failure came from an overly strict button selector rejecting a decorative `▶` before Play. The checker now accepts such prefixes. This trial also exposed a planning issue: a semicolon-separated list was stored as one step, so completing the scaffold marked the entire plan done. Planning now accepts that list format, while preserving punctuation inside explicit multiline steps, and infers `set` when an otherwise valid steps string omits the action. Regression coverage reproduces that exact failure.

## Changes under test::5.content:
Subsequent trials allow 12 acceptance checks, configured before their single launch. The public CLI exposes the existing agent setting as `--verify-attempts`; its default remains six. Assertions now name failed save-state fields and report observed coordinates when landing or New World movement fails. These changes improve repair feedback without relaxing gameplay requirements. The working control again passed all 12 production-preview groups (`control-final-feedback`).

LM Studio `verified-v5` finished incomplete after 1,495 seconds, 244 coding requests, 284 model tool calls and 12 failed checks. It repaired its own tests and several startup errors, but placement still failed. A separate observation-only browser diagnostic found that right-button press placed a block, then a trusted right-button `click` event removed it. The application's click handler did not distinguish buttons. The checker now reports changed-cell counts after press and release plus the actual mouse-event sequence. The control passed again (`control-event-feedback`), and the failed artifact reproduced the same placement failure with this more precise output. No game source was repaired by the supervisor.

This run also spent its first five acceptance attempts while still repairing project tests. Before final acceptance has started, recovery from repeated tools now reruns a known failing project check without spending the final acceptance budget. Once final acceptance starts, its failures remain authoritative. The caller's private command stays in the host/UI instead of model context, avoiding repeated attempts to invoke an inaccessible path. Regression tests verify both behaviors.

The next fresh pair uses a 65,536-token allocation, reasoning off, and 12 acceptance attempts. This explicitly tests a larger local working window after the 32k runs repeatedly churned through module interfaces. The allocation is recorded per run and is not evidence of a 32k success. The same gameplay requirements and current checker apply to both providers.

## Changes under test::6.content:
Ollama `verified-v6` returned completion in 1,469 seconds: 277 coding requests, 285 model tool calls, 86,030 generated tokens, six implementation checks and nine acceptance attempts. Its 27 project tests, production build and all 12 then-existing browser groups passed. Fresh browser sessions repeated those 12 groups successfully both inside the preview and at the direct URL. No game source was edited by the supervisor and no follow-up prompt was sent to the coding agent. However, visual inspection then found malformed terrain faces. This is a behavioral-check pass, **not an accepted finished game**.

During its targeting repairs, the checker error was expanded to include the actual snapshot and expected target shape. The game returned `{}` instead of coordinates, but the previous message only said that no terrain was targeted. The assertions were unchanged; attempts 1–3 used the earlier diagnostic, and attempt 4 onward used the new checker hash. The control passed again (`control-target-feedback`). Ollama then repaired the debug shape, pause menu and saved edit counter automatically. Its own reproduction scripts also caused wasted work and temporary UI regressions. A passing final result does not make that repair overhead efficient.

The missing graphics assertion now observes position, normal and index buffers actually submitted in WebGL draw calls, without relying on the game's debug API. It checks sampled triangle geometry against the supplied outward normals, exposing degenerate, reversed and misconstructed faces. The failed artifact reproduces 6,434 invalid sampled triangles (`ollama-v6-mesh-regression`), and the working control passes all **13** groups (`control-mesh-audit`). Seven independent WebGL fixtures cover valid indexed, nonindexed, interleaved and instanced data, plus incorrect normals, reversed winding and degenerate geometry. The observer only mirrors uploaded data; it never changes game geometry or input.

## Changes under test::7.content:
LM Studio `verified-v6` receives this thirteenth assertion before its first acceptance attempt. Ollama requires a new fresh trial with the stronger checker; continuing its already completed run with a repair prompt would not satisfy the single-launch requirement. Screenshots remain part of the supervising audit because geometry and pixel-diversity assertions cannot establish visual quality by themselves.

LM Studio `verified-v6` then completed in **826 seconds**, with 165 coding requests, 166 model tool calls, 51,289 generated tokens, five progress checks and five acceptance attempts. All 41 project tests, the production build and all 13 browser groups passed. The first acceptance failure was an inconsistent debug encoding (selected block name versus numeric world type); subsequent repairs fixed a pause overlay blocking Save and persistence of the edit counter. The supervisor did not modify game files or send a follow-up prompt. Two fresh browser sessions repeated all 13 groups successfully, inside the preview and at the direct URL. Visual inspection shows intact voxel terrain and trees.

The exact [LM Studio game source](evidence/lmstudio-block-meadow.zip) and [gameplay screenshot](evidence/lmstudio-game.png) are retained. Extract the source, then run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` in that directory. The source archive excludes dependencies, generated bundles and scratch investigations.

Ollama `verified-v7` used the fixed 13-group checker from launch but failed after 1,052 seconds, 291 coding requests, 284 model tool calls and 12 acceptance attempts. It eventually repaired mining's reported edit counter, then introduced a Play regression and repeatedly failed pause/resume. It retained the false assumption that headless pointer lock should be bypassed despite actual browser evidence. No checker changes, game edits or follow-up prompts were supplied by the supervisor during this trial.

## Changes under test::8.content:
The following harness revision adds a facts-only context refresh after two consecutive equivalent acceptance failures in a fresh conversation. It retains the task, plan/checkpoint, touched files and actual output while discarding previous model-written summaries and superseded investigation history. Repeat detection ignores numeric/whitespace variation without altering the evidence. A different failure keeps the current context. Sessions with earlier user turns retain ordinary compaction, protecting prior user decisions that may exist only in their summaries. Three integration tests cover changing observed values, preservation of raw evidence and the request, no extra inference, advancing checks, and protection of previous conversation summaries. The acceptance budget remains unchanged. New trials are needed to test this revision through both providers; the earlier LM Studio pass remains evidence for its recorded build.

Ollama `verified-v8` returned completion in 297 seconds: 69 coding requests, 65 model tool calls, 26,985 generated tokens, two progress checks and four acceptance attempts. All 13 then-existing browser groups passed, but visual inspection found that its crosshair, hotbar and FPS stayed hidden during play. The UI read a captured `active: false` value instead of live state. This is another rejected finished-game result. No source was repaired or follow-up prompt sent. The new repeated-failure refresh did not activate in this run, so its shorter time cannot be attributed to that mechanism.

## Changes under test::9.content:
The checker now adds a fourteenth group for visible gameplay controls and checks selection highlighting after each number key, plus HUD visibility after reload and New World. Eight positive/negative browser fixtures verify detection of hidden, transparent, offscreen and incomplete controls, a stopped FPS display and stale selection. It rejects the unchanged Ollama v8 artifact with the actual hidden layout. New tasks explicitly request accessible HTML HUD elements and selectable buttons. The older LM v6 artifact used differently named div cells, so this new selector contract does not retrospectively establish a HUD defect in that game. The working control passes the new HUD and selection assertions; a separate random-terrain targeting miss in that check run is retained as a failed run, not suppressed.

Ollama v8 also encoded a multiline plan with literal escaped newline text, which produced one oversized step. The tool's creation example now demonstrates plain semicolons, already supported by the parser. This changes the example rather than adding ambiguous escape decoding. Fresh Ollama v9 and LM Studio v7 trials use the same compiled harness, revised prompt and fourteen-group checker from launch.

Ollama `verified-v9` completed in **261 seconds**, with 65 coding requests, 63 model tool calls, 29,496 generated tokens, two project checks and two acceptance attempts. All **28 project tests**, the production build and all **14 gameplay groups** passed. The only final-gate repair aligned the debug selection encoding with the actual numeric world type. Fresh direct and embedded-preview sessions both repeated all fourteen groups successfully. Screenshots show intact terrain and trees, the crosshair, FPS and a changing hotbar highlight. No game-source edits, follow-up prompts or resumes were supplied by the supervisor. No compaction or facts-only refresh was needed in this run; three optional summary requests produced no applied summary.

## Changes under test::10.content:
The exact [Ollama v9 source](evidence/ollama-v9-block-meadow.zip) and [gameplay screenshot](evidence/ollama-game.png) are retained. Its numbered hotbar is functional but visually basic. This selected successful run follows the failed development trials above and does not establish a completion rate.

All 16 files in the Ollama archive match the generated workspace byte for byte. A clean extraction also passed `npm ci`, all 28 tests and the production build. The archive retains the model's Vite 5 toolchain: npm reported two vulnerable development dependencies, including a [Vite development-server advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff). These archives are exact benchmark records, not production deployment packages. The harness gains no runtime dependency from them.

LM Studio `verified-v7` completed its attempt budget **incomplete** after 1,743 seconds, 332 coding requests, 347 model tool calls and 92,328 generated tokens. It used three implementation checks and twelve acceptance attempts. It repaired lost fast clicks and pause/resume, but manual Save remained broken. Two facts-only refreshes occurred. The provider and harness stayed running through the trial, then the harness exited nonzero with the remaining failure; the supervisor did not edit game source or send a repair prompt.

## Changes under test::11.content:
This failure exposed missing diagnostic evidence in the browser gate. The game caught its Save exception and logged it with `console.error`, which the checker did not collect. The report said no uncaught exceptions and omitted the actual `setItem is not a function` error. Read-only reproduction on the unchanged failed artifact now includes that error (`lm-v7-console-regression`). A browser fixture verifies caught-error capture, duplicate suppression and bounded storage. Failure feedback also retains the already-passed behaviors, and mining failures include actual target/block values and trusted mouse events with pointer-lock state. The fourteen behavioral assertions are unchanged.

Fresh LM Studio v8 uses these diagnostics from launch, with the same compiled harness, task prompt, model allocation and attempt budget as Ollama v9. The two original checker hashes therefore differ; this is recorded explicitly, not treated as a controlled measurement of diagnostic effectiveness. The accepted Ollama artifact is independently rerun through the updated checker at its direct static URL and through the embedded preview. No code in that game is changed.

LM Studio `verified-v8` returned completion after **896 seconds**, with 145 coding requests, 142 model tool calls, 51,719 generated tokens, four project checks and three acceptance attempts. It repaired reversed mesh faces and an overlay intercepting Save. Fourteen project tests and all fourteen embedded-preview groups passed, and a fresh preview repeat passed too. **The direct-browser repeat failed save/reload**, however: loading beside an adjacent placed block moved the player from y=21 to the default y=24.5 spawn. Its restore check rejected every solid in a 3×3 neighborhood, including blocks outside the player's actual body. The different view produced a nearer valid placement and exposed this bug. This artifact is rejected as a finished-game pass. Its unchanged [source archive](evidence/lmstudio-v8-block-meadow.zip) also passes a clean install, project tests and build, demonstrating why those checks are insufficient.

## Changes under test::12.content:
The acceptance command now runs the entire lifecycle in **both** the embedded preview and a direct browser before returning success: fourteen groups per view, twenty-eight checks total. A failure in either returns to the still-running agent. The unchanged failed LM v8 game reproduces the direct-view failure (`lm-v8-dual-regression`), while the accepted Ollama v9 game passes all twenty-eight (`ollama-v9-dual-final`). LM Studio v9 begins a fresh task with this combined gate. No repair prompt is sent to the completed v8 agent and no generated source is edited by the supervisor.

LM Studio `verified-v9` returned completion after **1,422 seconds**, with 289 coding requests, 305 model tool calls, 89,885 generated tokens, six project checks and nine acceptance attempts. It repaired startup, the Save overlay and restoring player state before Play. All twenty-eight then-existing checks passed, but independent source review and browser reproduction found a further **rendering failure**. Play created a new world for collision and editing while the renderer retained the menu's original world. A fresh direct session showed 13,414 differing terrain cells between those objects. Mining modified live terrain but rebuilt geometry from the stale world. This game is rejected as a finished result despite its passing state assertions.

## Changes under test::13.content:
The WebGL observer now fingerprints the geometry actually drawn, including instance transforms and draw counts. Mining and placement must change both live terrain and rendered geometry. Re-uploading identical stale data does not qualify. Six positive/negative fixtures cover unchanged frames, identical rebuilds, changed positions, indices, instance transforms and instance counts; the seven existing triangle fixtures also pass. The unchanged LM v9 game fails this strengthened gate at mining (`lm-v9-render-regression`). This observes actual drawing without depending on the generated game's internal object names. The read-only object comparison is retained separately as corroborating evidence. Fresh LM Studio v10 uses the strengthened gate from launch; no game source is repaired or prior trial resumed by the supervisor.

LM Studio `verified-v10` returned completion after **959 seconds**, with 223 coding requests, 224 model tool calls, 60,276 generated tokens and six acceptance attempts. It repaired startup, mesh winding and the renderer callback. All twenty-eight then-existing groups passed, including visible editing. Independent checks at rotated headings found a **strafe-direction bug**, however: its right vector used the wrong sine sign, so forward and sideways movement were not perpendicular after turning. The earlier movement check only verified displacement at the starting heading. The unchanged game fails the stronger control check both directly (`lm-v10-heading`) and through the combined gate (`lm-v10-heading-regression`). This is another rejected finished-game result.

## Changes under test::14.content:
The final movement check exercises all four keys at three headings, requiring opposite forward/back and left/right directions, perpendicular strafing, and a heading change after real mouse movement. Positive/negative basis fixtures and the unchanged Ollama v9 game verify the check. The gate also mines a visible block after New World and recovers from two malformed-save cases, for **fifteen groups per view, thirty total**. Geometry comparison now uses the current drawn frame so valid rebuilding of previously seen terrain still counts as a visible change; fixtures cover identical rebuilds, changed frames and restored frames. LM Studio v11 starts fresh with this gate. The compiled harness and task prompt remain unchanged.

LM Studio `verified-v11` completed in **937 seconds**, generating 55,875 tokens across 187 coding requests and 195 model tool calls. It used five project checks and five acceptance attempts. The first two attempts exposed a frozen FPS display; the third reached New World but could not finish it. The fourth passed all thirty groups, and the fifth passed again after the agent completed its plan and reran project checks. One facts-only refresh retained the actual FPS failure, alongside four ordinary evictions. Eight optional summary requests produced no applied model summary. An independent thirty-group repeat also passed, and visual inspection showed intact terrain, trees, the crosshair, FPS and labeled hotbar. Camera, raycast and movement headings were also checked in source. Its eighteen-file archive matches the generated source byte for byte and passes a clean install, all twenty-three project tests and the production build.

- **Zéro code tronqué / Zéro placeholder :** Interdiction stricte de laisser des "TODO", "mock", "implémentation future" ou du code tronqué. Tout code produit est complet, typé, robuste et prêt pour la production.

## 2. D\u00e9roulement M\u00e9thodique p.content:
## 2. Déroulement Méthodique par Étape

Pour toute tâche complexe, suivre rigoureusement ce cycle :

1. **Planification (`plan`) :** Définir 3 à 5 étapes atomiques (`plan` action `set`).
2. **Investigation (`read_file` / `search`) :** Lire les fichiers concernés et repérer les points d'ancrage.
3. **Action ciblée (`edit_file` / `write_file`) :** Implémenter une seule modification cohérente à la fois.
4. **Vérification immédiate (`run_command`) :** Valider la syntaxe et lancer les tests.
5. **Validation du jalon (`plan` action `done`) :** Marquer l'étape franchie avant de passer à la suivante.

## 6. Protocole Multi-Sous-Agents & TDD (Standard Claude Code & Codex)

Pour atteindre le niveau d'excellence de Claude Code et Codex, smolcoder applique ce protocole :

- **Cycle TDD (Test-Driven Development) :** Rédiger systématiquement le test unitaire avant d'implémenter la logique métier. Exécuter le test, vérifier son échec initial, implémenter le code puis valider son succès.

## 7. Alignement d'Architecture Entreprise (Standard Oracle Fusion AI)

smolcoder applique rigoureusement les 4 piliers d'excellence d'[Oracle Fusion AI](https://www.oracle.com/applications/fusion-ai/) :

1. **Intégration Native (« Built-in, not bolted-on ») :** Les 6 nouveaux outils (`memory`, `subagent`, `skill`, `web_fetch`, `think`, `mcp_call`) sont intégrés directement dans le moteur d'exécution natif, partageant le même modèle de données et contexte que smolcoder.
2. **Orchestration de Bout en Bout (« End-to-End Workflows ») :** Division méthodique des tâches complexes entre sous-agents spécialisés (`architect`, `implementer`, `spec_reviewer`, `quality_reviewer`) synchronisés par la boucle fermée de vérification `--verify`.
3. **Gouvernance et Sécurité Stricte (« Security & Governance ») :** Blocage formel du serveur MCP Git pour éliminer tout risque d'exfiltration ou d'écrasement incontrôlé ; auditabilité absolue garantie par les points de sauvegarde silencieux `[Auto-Checkpoint]` à chaque modification.
4. **Mémoire Contextuelle Partagée (« Shared Context & Memory ») :** Conservation illimitée des faits clés, décisions d'architecture et règles projet dans la base vectorielle locale ChromaDB (`memory`), accessible à travers toutes les sessions sans perte d'historique.

# Architecture Entreprise : Alignement sur les 4 Piliers Oracle Fusion AI

Ce document détaille la transposition des principes d'architecture d'[Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications AI](https://www.oracle.com/applications/fusion-ai/) au sein de l'écosystème autonome de smolcoder.

---

## 1. Vue d'Ensemble & Philosophie.content:
## 1. Vue d'Ensemble & Philosophie

Oracle Fusion AI postule que pour être efficace, fiable et sécurisée en environnement critique, l'intelligence artificielle ne doit pas être un module rapporté (« bolted on »), mais faire corps avec le moteur d'exécution (« built in »), en partageant le même modèle de données, les mêmes garde-fous de sécurité et la même mémoire continue.

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   SMOLCODER ENTERPRISE RUNTIME                         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. BUILT-IN ENGINE      │ 14 Outils natifs (ChromaDB, MCP, Subagents) │
│  2. END-TO-END WORKFLOWS │ Orchestration Multi-Agents & Boucle --verify│
│  3. STRICT GOVERNANCE    │ Blocage MCP Git + Git Auto-Checkpoints      │
│  4. SHARED CONTEXT       │ Mémoire Vectorielle Infinie ChromaDB        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Pilier 1 : Intégration Native (« Built-in, not bolted-on »)

- **Principe Oracle :** Les capacités de raisonnement et d'exécution partagent directement la pile technologique et le contexte de l'application sans passer par des connecteurs intermédiaires instables.
- **Implémentation Smolcoder :**
  Les 6 outils d'extension (`memory`, `subagent`, `skill`, `web_fetch`, `think`, `mcp_call`) sont injectés directement dans le fichier compilé `dist/tools/index.js`. Ils disposent d'un accès natif au contexte de session (`ctx.workspace`, `ctx.filesTouched`, `ctx.plan`) et s'exécutent avec des performances instantanées.

### Pilier 2 : Orchestration de Bout en Bout (« End-to-End Workflows »)

- **Principe Oracle :** Les agents ne se limitent pas à générer du texte ; ils accomplissent des processus complets avec validation et correction autonome.
- **Implémentation Smolcoder :**
  Délégation du travail via l'outil `subagent` vers 4 rôles spécialisés :
  1. `architect` : Analyse de dépendances et spécification des interfaces.
  2. `implementer` : Développement rigoureux en TDD (Test-Driven Development).
  3. `spec_reviewer` : Contrôle de conformité par rapport au besoin.
  4. `quality_reviewer` : Audit de résilience, gestion des cas limites et linting.
  La boucle `--verify` exécute les tests en continu jusqu'au succès complet.

### Pilier 3 : Gouvernance et Sécurité Stricte (« Security & Governance »)

- **Principe Oracle :** Contrôle des accès, isolation des environnements et traçabilité inviolable (audit trail).
- **Implémentation Smolcoder :**
  - **Exclusion stricte du serveur MCP Git :** Bloqué au niveau de la passerelle `mcp-bridge.js` pour empêcher toute corruption ou exfiltration de dépôt.
  - **Machine à remonter le temps Git :** Chaque modification via `write_file` ou `edit_file` déclenche un commit silencieux `[Auto-Checkpoint]` permettant un rollback instantané.
  - **Auto-Linter instantané :** Biome (JS/TS) et Ruff (Python) valident et corrigent le code à chaque écriture.

# Mémoire durable du projet

- L’utilisateur veut faire évoluer Smolcoder vers un IDE professionnel, dans ses trois interfaces : terminal/CLI, application de bureau Electron et interface web.
- Vision durable élargie : réunir un IDE et un harnais de codage de niveau professionnel, un assistant de travail et de vie quotidienne (type Cowork), et un SmolClaw unifié ; couvrir progressivement les métiers d’entreprise, Microsoft Office, bibliothèques, skills, outils, MCP et sous-agents réellement disponibles.
- Construire ces capacités de manière intégrée et multi-interface, par incréments solides, avec une expérience accessible à une personne débutante ; distinguer clairement les intégrations disponibles de celles qui restent à créer/configurer.
- Pour le volet Cowork inspiré des outils professionnels 2026 : tâches longues visibles et reprenables, rôles spécialisés avec permissions réellement appliquées, skills/connecteurs configurables, et demande d’accord humain avant toute action externe en mode édition.
- Les plans du harnais doivent aussi survivre aux redémarrages : clés isolées par conversation Web, et reprise stable dans le CLI/headless sans mélanger les agents parallèles.
- Conserver les réglages de raisonnement séparément pour Ollama et LM Studio ; ne pas écraser les préférences d’un serveur lorsqu’on bascule vers l’autre.
- Le harnais de validation doit découvrir les tests des principaux écosystèmes (pas seulement Node) avec des commandes conventionnelles bornées et sans exécuter de scripts arbitraires lus dans les manifestes.

Toujours demander avant d'agir ; un lot groupé d'actions peut être proposé et exécuté si l'utilisateur répond oui. Même avec la règle AGENTS.md qui exige `npm run build` après toute modification TypeScript : l'annoncer d'abord à l'utilisateur.
- Prochaines corrections prioritaires (convenues, 2026-09-27) : 1) tester un scénario réel complet dans le web et Electron (modifier un fichier → lancer le build → corriger l'erreur → afficher le résultat) ; 2) créer un panneau MCP permettant de relancer individuellement un serveur en erreur ; 3) connecter réellement C3 à ses actions mémoire/indexation au lieu de seulement afficher sa présence ; 4) enrichir Cowork avec des actions métier pilotées par les MCP effectivement disponibles ; 5) ajouter un vrai aperçu local du workspace, pas seulement un aperçu d'URL externe.

Restants du vieux plan : fixer le test flaky `test/verification.test.js:101` (« recovery from failed edits… », race sur ready.txt, verify.cjs exit 42), synthèse finale FR simple, vérifier les changements codex + fraîcheur dist/ vs src/ + répondre au 524 Cloudflare/Ollama. Dépôt : main en avance de 8 commits sur origin/main ; `dist/` frais ; localisation « 1 Mo » cohérente entre src/editor-tools.ts et test.
- Priorités : corriger les problèmes réels, enrichir les fonctions de codage et l’expérience d’édition, garder la coloration syntaxique des réponses de code dans toutes les interfaces, et vérifier les changements avec des tests.
- L’analyse LSP des fichiers TypeScript/JavaScript est désormais visible dans les éditeurs Web et Electron à l’ouverture et après enregistrement ; les problèmes sont sélectionnables et la navigation reste bornée au projet. Étendre ensuite les diagnostics à d’autres langages et améliorer l’édition avancée sans installer silencieusement de dépendances.
- L’utilisateur débute en informatique : expliquer les résultats en français simple, ne pas lui transférer les décisions techniques ordinaires et ne pas prétendre que Smolcoder égale déjà les IDE établis tant que cela n’est pas démontré.

staged (they stay put). Hunks outside the selection keep the index as-is.
Pure (exported for tests).

code 0 = body in out, code 1 + empty out = strings are identical,
code 2 = error message in out. Never throws.

git computes the patch itself — positions are always honest, never
hand-counted. Never throws.
